title: Review: Polarisation; Reflection and refraction; Total internal reflection and optical fibres; Single-slit diffraction; Superposition, interference and coherence
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-1#N.9a, W05-1#N.5a, W06-1#N.2a, W08-1#N.12, W04-1#N.6a, W05-1#N.3a, W06-1#N.12, W05-1#N.14a, W06-1#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ray
items.clue: Line perpendicular to the wavefronts, showing the direction the energy travels.

items.label: Refraction
items.clue: Change in direction as a transmitted wave changes speed on crossing a boundary at an angle.

items.label: Normal
items.clue: Line at 90° to a surface at the point where light meets it; every angle is measured from it.

items.label: Total internal reflection
items.clue: Beyond a certain incidence, no light passes into the lower-n medium: all of it bounces back.

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?
A glass block of refractive index 1.52 is under water of refractive index 1.33. A ray inside the glass meets the glass–water boundary at an angle of incidence of 55.0°. What happens to the ray?

options.text: It is totally internally reflected, as 55.0° is more than 41.1°.
It refracts into the water at 69.4° to the normal.
It refracts into the water at 45.8° to the normal.
It passes into the water at 55.0°, without bending.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.33/1.52) = 61.0°, and 55.0° < 61.0°, so it refracts: 1.52 sin 55.0° = 1.33 sin θ₂, θ₂ = 69.4°.

questions.stem: Two pulses of identical shape and size but opposite displacement travel towards each other along a stretched string. At one instant they overlap exactly and the whole string is momentarily straight. Which statement about this instant, and what follows it, is correct?

options.text: The pulses have cancelled each other out; the string stays straight from now on.
The string is straight but moving; the pulses then emerge and continue past each other.
The string is straight and at rest; the pulses' energy has become internal energy of the string.
The pulses have collided; each then travels back the way it came, with its shape restored.

questions.stem: Sea waves reach a harbour wall with a 20 m wide entrance. A boat is moored behind the wall, well to one side of the entrance. On day 1 the waves have a wavelength of 20 m; on day 2, 2.0 m, with the same amplitude. On which day is the boat rocked more, and why?

options.text: Day 1: the wavelength is about the width of the gap, so the waves spread widely.
Day 2: shorter waves have a higher frequency, so they carry more energy around the wall.
Neither: the gap is the same width both days, and the gap alone sets the spreading.
Day 2: shorter waves fit through the gap more easily, so more of them pass behind it.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Light can cross a flat boundary between water (n = 1.33) and glass (n = 1.50) in either direction. Which statement about total internal reflection at this boundary is correct?

options.text: It can occur for light in the glass heading towards the water.
It can occur for light that is in the water and heading towards the glass.
It can occur for light going either way, if the angle is large enough.
It needs air beyond the boundary, so it does not occur at this one.

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light heading into a lower refractive index: here, light in the glass (1.50) meeting the water (1.33), at angles of incidence above sin⁻¹(1.33/1.50), about 62°.

questions.stem: Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ

questions.stem: An optical fibre has a glass core of refractive index 1.50, surrounded by glass of refractive index 1.40. On a straight stretch, a ray meets the core's wall at 75° to the normal. Where the fibre bends, the same ray meets the wall at 66° to the normal. What happens at each point?

options.text: Trapped at both: once light is inside the core, it cannot leave.
Totally internally reflected at 75°; at 66° some light passes out of the core.
Totally internally reflected at both, as both angles are more than 41.8°.
Some light passes out at 75°, but the ray is trapped at 66°.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.40/1.50) = 69.0°. 75° > 69.0°: TIR. 66° < 69.0°: part of the light refracts out (at 78° to the normal). A sharp bend lets light leak.

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.
